question.text: Vindhya Event-Driven Fund received unlisted shares as part of a distressed-arb deal at INR 40 lakh where FMV per prescribed rules was INR 60 lakh. Under Section 56(2)(x) (deemed income from inadequate consideration) and the workbook's effective rate of 34.944% for 'other investors', the tax impact on the deemed income is:

answer.text: Nil — Section 56(2)(x) does not apply to AIFs
INR 6,98,880 (34.944% on the shortfall of INR 20 lakh)

explanation.text: The Logic: Shortfall = FMV INR 60 lakh - consideration INR 40 lakh = INR 20 lakh, which exceeds the INR 0.05 million threshold in Section 56(2)(x). The fund is treated as an 'other investor' (trust), and the workbook's effective rate table gives 34.944% for that class. Tax = 20,00,000 x 34.944% = INR 6,98,880. The Trap: Option A is false because Section 56(2)(x) applies to any acquirer, including AIFs. Option B uses a fictional 10% rate that has no basis in the workbook. Option C applies the 42.744% individual/HUF rate to a trust assessee. Note: FMV for Section 56(2)(x) is determined under the prescribed rules, so contemporaneous valuation documentation is important whenever shares are acquired below the prescribed FMV.
